attractions.name: Bob Marley Museum, Kingston
attractions.desc: Bob Marley's former Kingston home, now preserved much as he left it, including the room where he was shot during a 1976 assassination attempt. Guided tours cover his life, his music, and reggae's rise from Jamaican dance halls to a global genre. It anchors Kingston's Trench Town and uptown music heritage sites for visitors wanting to go deeper into the island's musical roots.

attractions.name: Dunn's River Falls
attractions.desc: A 180-meter terraced waterfall near Ocho Rios that visitors climb hand-in-hand in guided human chains, the cascading limestone steps forming natural pools along the way. It empties directly onto a beach, making a post-climb swim in the sea a natural finish. It's one of the most visited sights in Jamaica and can get crowded when cruise ships are in port, so an early start helps.

attractions.name: Blue Mountains
attractions.desc: A misty mountain range east of Kingston that produces Blue Mountain coffee, among the most sought-after and expensive coffee in the world, grown on steep, cloud-covered slopes above 1,500 meters. Coffee farm tours explain the whole process from bean to cup, and a pre-dawn hike up Blue Mountain Peak rewards early risers with sunrise views stretching to Cuba on a clear day. The cooler mountain air is a welcome break from the coastal heat.

attractions.name: Negril's Seven Mile Beach
attractions.desc: A long, uninterrupted stretch of white sand on Jamaica's western tip, backed by a laid-back beach-town scene of reggae bars and sunset-watching rituals at the cliffs further along the coast. Negril grew out of a 1970s hippie trail and still carries a slower, less resort-heavy feel than Montego Bay or Ocho Rios. Cliff diving at Rick's Cafe is a well-known sunset tradition for visitors and locals alike.

attractions.name: YS Falls
attractions.desc: A series of cascading waterfalls and swimming pools on the south coast, reached by a short tractor-drawn cart ride through a working cattle farm before the trail begins. A rope swing and small zipline add a bit of adventure alongside the swimming, and the south coast's generally quieter, less touristed feel extends to the falls themselves. It's a good day trip pairing with the nearby Black River safari for crocodile spotting.

attractions.name: Jerk cooking heritage (Boston Bay)
attractions.desc: Boston Bay, on Jamaica's northeast coast, is widely considered the birthplace of jerk cooking, where roadside pits still smoke chicken and pork over pimento wood using techniques passed down for generations. The seasoning blend of scotch bonnet peppers, allspice, and thyme is fiercely guarded and varies from pit to pit. Eating jerk here, standing at a roadside stall rather than a restaurant, is considered by many the definitive way to experience it.

itinerary.label: Days 1–2
itinerary.title: Kingston & the Blue Mountains
itinerary.desc: Reggae heritage sites and a coffee-country detour into the misty mountains.
itinerary.logistics: Norman Manley International Airport is ~20 min from central Kingston
itinerary.food: Try ackee and saltfish, Jamaica's national dish, at a local breakfast spot in Kingston.

itinerary.label: Days 3–4
itinerary.title: Ocho Rios
itinerary.desc: Dunn's River Falls and the north coast's classic waterfall-and-beach combination.
itinerary.food: Try jerk chicken at a roadside stall along the north coast highway.

itinerary.label: Days 5–7
itinerary.title: Negril
itinerary.desc: Seven Mile Beach, cliff-diving sunsets, and a slower island pace to close the trip.
itinerary.logistics: ~2h drive from Ocho Rios along the north coast
itinerary.food: Try fresh grilled lobster at a beachfront shack in Negril.

goodToKnow.tipping: 10-15% in restaurants is standard, sometimes added automatically as a service charge
goodToKnow.safety: Generally safe for tourists in resort areas and main tourist zones; standard caution advised in parts of Kingston, especially at night
goodToKnow.gettingAround: A rental car or private driver is the most flexible way to see the island; resort areas are also well served by organized tours
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Montego Bay's Sangster International Airport (MBJ) serves most north-coast resorts, with Kingston's Norman Manley International (KIN) better for the capital and Blue Mountains

food.name: Jerk chicken
food.desc: Chicken marinated in a fiery scotch bonnet and allspice blend, traditionally smoked over pimento wood.

food.name: Ackee and saltfish
food.desc: Jamaica's national dish: a buttery fruit sautéed with salted, rehydrated codfish, onion, and pepper.

food.name: Patties
food.desc: Flaky, curry-colored pastries filled with spiced meat or vegetables, a beloved grab-and-go snack.

food.name: Blue Mountain coffee
food.desc: Smooth, mild coffee grown only on the island's misty Blue Mountain slopes, among the world's most prized.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Jamaica?
faq.a: Not for EU, UK, US, and most Commonwealth passport holders for short tourist stays — always confirm current rules before booking.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Montego Bay's Sangster International (MBJ) for the north coast resorts, or Kingston's Norman Manley International (KIN) for the capital and Blue Mountains.

faq.q: Is Jamaica just resorts, or is independent travel easy too?
faq.a: Both work well — all-inclusive resorts are common and convenient, but independent travel by rental car or organized day tours between towns is also straightforward.

faq.q: Is Blue Mountain coffee really worth the price?
faq.a: It's genuinely limited in supply and distinct in flavor, which drives the price — whether it's 'worth it' is subjective, but a farm tour and fresh cup in the mountains is a worthwhile experience regardless.

daysReason: 7 days covers Kingston's music heritage, a mountain detour, and beach time on the north coast without rushing. 4–5 days works for a north-coast-only trip; 10 lets you add the quieter south coast around YS Falls.
visa: Not required for EU, UK, US, and most Commonwealth passport holders for short tourist stays — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Museu Bob Marley, Kingston
attractions.desc: A antiga casa de Bob Marley em Kingston, hoje preservada tal como ele a deixou, incluindo o quarto onde foi baleado durante uma tentativa de assassinato em 1976. Visitas guiadas cobrem a sua vida, a sua música, e a ascensão do reggae das salas de baile jamaicanas a um género global. Ancora os locais de património musical de Trench Town e da zona alta de Kingston para visitantes que querem aprofundar as raízes musicais da ilha.

attractions.name: Dunn's River Falls
attractions.desc: Uma cascata em socalcos de 180 metros perto de Ocho Rios que os visitantes sobem de mãos dadas em correntes humanas guiadas, os degraus calcários em cascata a formar piscinas naturais pelo caminho. Desagua diretamente numa praia, tornando um mergulho no mar após a subida um final natural. É um dos locais mais visitados da Jamaica e pode ficar cheio quando há cruzeiros no porto, por isso começar cedo ajuda.

attractions.name: Blue Mountains
attractions.desc: Uma cordilheira enevoada a leste de Kingston que produz o café Blue Mountain, entre os cafés mais cobiçados e caros do mundo, cultivado em encostas íngremes e cobertas de nuvens acima dos 1.500 metros. Visitas a quintas de café explicam todo o processo do grão à chávena, e uma caminhada antes do amanhecer até ao Pico Blue Mountain recompensa os madrugadores com vistas do nascer do sol que se estendem até Cuba num dia limpo. O ar mais fresco da montanha é uma pausa bem-vinda do calor costeiro.

attractions.name: Seven Mile Beach, Negril
attractions.desc: Uma longa e ininterrupta faixa de areia branca na ponta ocidental da Jamaica, sustentada por um ambiente descontraído de vila de praia com bares de reggae e rituais de observação do pôr do sol nas falésias mais adiante na costa. Negril nasceu de uma rota hippie dos anos 1970 e ainda tem um ambiente mais lento e menos dominado por resorts do que Montego Bay ou Ocho Rios. Saltar das falésias no Rick's Cafe é uma conhecida tradição de pôr do sol para visitantes e locais.

attractions.name: YS Falls
attractions.desc: Uma série de cascatas e piscinas naturais na costa sul, alcançadas por um curto passeio de carroça puxada por trator através de uma quinta de gado em funcionamento antes de o trilho começar. Uma corda para balançar e uma pequena tirolesa acrescentam um pouco de aventura ao lado da natação, e o ambiente geralmente mais tranquilo e menos turístico da costa sul estende-se às próprias cascatas. É uma boa excursão de um dia combinada com o vizinho safari do Rio Black para avistar crocodilos.

attractions.name: Património da cozinha jerk (Boston Bay)
attractions.desc: Boston Bay, na costa nordeste da Jamaica, é amplamente considerada o berço da cozinha jerk, onde fossas à beira da estrada ainda fumam frango e porco sobre madeira de pimenteira usando técnicas transmitidas ao longo de gerações. A mistura de tempero de pimenta scotch bonnet, pimenta-da-jamaica e tomilho é ferozmente guardada e varia de fossa para fossa. Comer jerk aqui, de pé numa banca à beira da estrada em vez de num restaurante, é considerado por muitos a forma definitiva de o experienciar.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–2
itinerary.title: Kingston e Blue Mountains
itinerary.desc: Locais de património do reggae e um desvio à terra do café nas montanhas enevoadas.
itinerary.logistics: O Aeroporto Internacional Norman Manley fica a ~20 min do centro de Kingston

itinerary.label: Dias 3–4
itinerary.title: Ocho Rios
itinerary.desc: Dunn's River Falls e a clássica combinação de cascata e praia da costa norte.

itinerary.label: Dias 5–7
itinerary.title: Negril
itinerary.desc: Seven Mile Beach, pores do sol com saltos de falésia, e um ritmo de ilha mais lento para fechar a viagem.
itinerary.logistics: ~2h de carro desde Ocho Rios pela costa norte

goodToKnow.tipping: 10-15% em restaurantes é padrão, por vezes já incluído como taxa de serviço
goodToKnow.safety: Geralmente seguro para turistas em zonas de resort e turísticas principais; recomenda-se cautela normal em partes de Kingston, especialmente à noite
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Um carro alugado ou motorista privado é a forma mais flexível de ver a ilha; as zonas de resort também são bem servidas por excursões organizadas
goodToKnow.gettingThere: O Aeroporto Internacional Sangster (MBJ), em Montego Bay, serve a maioria dos resorts da costa norte, com o Aeroporto Internacional Norman Manley (KIN), em Kingston, melhor para a capital e as Blue Mountains

food.name: Frango jerk
food.desc: Frango marinado numa mistura ardente de pimenta scotch bonnet e pimenta-da-jamaica, tradicionalmente fumado sobre madeira de pimenteira.

food.name: Ackee com bacalhau
food.desc: O prato nacional da Jamaica: um fruto amanteigado salteado com bacalhau salgado reidratado, cebola e pimento.

food.name: Patties
food.desc: Pastéis folhados de cor de caril recheados de carne ou vegetais especiados, um snack muito apreciado para levar.

food.name: Café Blue Mountain
food.desc: Café suave e macio cultivado só nas encostas enevoadas Blue Mountain da ilha, entre os mais valorizados do mundo.
